title: Chaos: the marks change the visual grammar of a shared base

observations.finding: Knight of Khorne · Axe and Knight of Khorne · Champion put the strongest red on the upright head crest, chest and weapon. Gold outlines separate these red fields from the dark hanging mail. Their outward shoulder spikes and near-rectangular crown forks make the upper silhouette read as a wide block with two vertical prongs. Both credit Vile Knight as their model base.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Knight of Nurgle, Heavy and Champion break that clean red-and-gold hierarchy with low-saturation olive plates, fleshy or mouth-like forms, irregular horns and much wider soft belly shapes. The credited sources explicitly include Ghoul/Abomination faces and a stone-deer statue for horns. A source object can therefore contribute its shape independently of the material painted on it.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Knight of Slaanesh · Axe and Lance retain the shared armoured base but the large purple cloth area, bright gold bands, tall delicate horn sweep and face-bearing shield make a different mark readable. The axe and lance variants share their major silhouette landmarks; the long lance adds reach without requiring a wholesale body redesign. Their total meshes are 2,504 and 2,366 triangles respectively.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Knight of Tzeentch · Sword/Lance and Warrior of Tzeentch use dark blue, cyan light, purple cloth and eyes as separate focal points. The visible eye animation is sourced from the Battle.net working animation texture series. The two knights each reference 30 eye-frame images; the warrior references 29. Counting those frames as unrelated painted materials exaggerates the number of visual ingredients.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Knight Undivided · Sword/Lance and Aspiring Champion place black or charcoal plate beneath gold rims, horns and repeated star motifs. The palette creates a shared visual relationship without needing the red Khorne fields, green Nurgle flesh or cyan Tzeentch eyes. The credits separately name helmets, shoulder stars, horns and a fur cloak.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Warrior of Khorne · Cleaver is 1,009 triangles while Berserker is 1,930 and Bruiser is 1,720. The cleaver still reads as the same heavily armoured family in the published pictures. The large continuous red blade carries much of its identity; total triangle count is not a direct measure of how ornate a character reads.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

limits: These are observations of the 20 catalogue Chaos models. They do not establish a required Chaos triangle budget. The knight credits include mounted-base and horse sources, so each actual surface must be identified before interpreting an armour fragment as human anatomy.

title: Vampire Counts: a faction built from deliberately different body types

observations.finding: Graveguard carries the undead identity with a concealed head, thin exposed bone, long polearm and ornate tall shield. Von Carstein Vampire and Von Carstein Dread Knight expose a pale face above upright plate and a long sword. Strigoi Vampire instead uses an enlarged muscular bare torso, long arms, claws and a dark animal-like face. Necrarch Vampire uses a hanging black robe and narrow exposed hands. These examples contradict a single universal vampire body proportion.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Von Carstein Vampire and Dread Knight both contain exactly 1,535 triangles, yet the catalogue has 30 versus 35 geosets and their files differ by 4,850 bytes. Their published images distinguish the cloth and armour treatment rather than a larger silhouette. Equal triangle totals therefore do not imply equal material partition or file contents.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Graveguard uses the Human campaign Footman, Human campaign tree, Undead inventory cover, Undead buildings and multiple creature sheets in one model. These are measured references in the actual MDX, not a list of suggested substitutes. Its credits name the shield as projected and the gargoyle head and helmet wings as Blizzard sources.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Blood Dragon concentrates red on the torso, shoulders and weapon while the limbs and hanging cloth stay dark. Its credited shoulder pads/breastplate come from a dragon-scale armour source, distinct from the skull belt, vampire face and helmet sources. In this collection the Blood Dragon silhouette is an armoured warrior, whereas the Strigoi silhouette is the body itself.

observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

limits: Only six Vampire Counts catalogue models are present. Skeleton ranks, cavalry formations and architecture cannot be inferred from this sample alone.

title: Empire: equipment and heraldry carry role recognition

observations.finding: Empire Captain, Halberdier and Swordsman combine a bright red cloth area with pale breastplate, a dark boot mass and a feather or plume high on the head. Shields carry broad readable cross divisions. The polearm and sword separate the role while the torso palette keeps the figures together.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Estalian Swordsman replaces the rectangular cross shield with a round concentric target, and Estalian Infantry/Spearman use a brimmed helmet rather than the same feathered profile. The distinctive equipment remains legible even though red, silver and brown remain shared colours.

observations.finding: Knight of the Blazing Sun uses the head-sized gold sun crest as its strongest identifying motif in both mounted and dismounted versions. The arquebus, flintlock, scoped and multi-barrel variants retain a compact human body, while barrel length, muzzle grouping and the sight create the visible differences. The mortar changes the barrel angle and opening into a squat bowl-like shape, making function visible in silhouette.

title: Bretonnia: three commoners, not a knight-based faction sample

observations.finding: Bretonnian Archer, Pikeman and Swordsman share blue upper clothing, brown wrapped boots, a large square belt buckle and a small gold chest emblem. The archer has a hood, the pikeman a simple helmet, and the swordsman a tall blue shield; headgear and held equipment distinguish the three roles.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: The visible body proportions remain short-legged and broad-booted across the three published pictures. The pike extends far above the head, while the bow and shield create lateral rather than vertical mass. Their whole-model totals are 783, 825 and 896 triangles respectively. These are measured commoner examples, not a proposed generic humanoid budget.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

limits: There are no Bretonnian knights, horses, nobles or buildings in this catalogue snapshot. A full Bretonnian silhouette profile would require additional permitted examples.

title: Dwarfs: artillery construction rather than humanoid proportions

observations.finding: Dwarf Cannon and all four Dwarf Organ Cannon versions use broad metal-covered wheels, low compact carriages, large muzzle openings, blue vertical bands and gold rings or face ornaments. The single cannon has one dominant barrel; the organ cannon has five aligned dark muzzles.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: All four organ-cannon variants have exactly 878 triangles, 14 geosets and three catalogue geoset texture references. Their filenames and sequence variants describe different firing patterns, and their MDX sizes range from 184,277 to 322,173 bytes. This is a direct example of file size varying greatly without a triangle-count change.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: The Dwarf Cannon is 582 triangles. In the pictures, the organ version changes not only the barrel count but also the central vertical rib mass. The repeated five-muzzle silhouette makes the extra 296 triangles visually intelligible.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

limits: All five Dwarf entries are artillery, and four are versions of one organ-cannon design. This set cannot support claims about dwarf body proportions, beards or infantry armour.

title: Skaven: hunched bodies, long tails and weapon-sized technology

observations.finding: Clanrat, Stormvermin, Warplock Jezzail and Ratling Gunner retain projecting snouts, bent-legged posture, thin segmented tails and small exposed feet. Green cloth ties the examples together while the body and hands remain a dirty brown or pale flesh colour.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: The Ratling Gunner’s back apparatus and multi-hole muzzle dominate the silhouette; its 1,890-triangle total is over twice the Clanrat’s 720. The Jezzail is between them at 1,085 triangles and emphasizes an exceptionally long firearm instead of a bulky pack. The examples show three different allocations of geometric effort to readable equipment.
observations.evidence: downloaded published model thumbnails plus actual parsed MDX metrics and catalogue credit statements
observations.certainty: observed; bounded to these named examples

observations.finding: Stormvermin raises the role with a broad upward-curving polearm blade, horned helmet and larger metal shoulder shape. Its 819 triangles remain much closer to Clanrat than to Ratling Gunner. The rank difference is concentrated in conspicuous extremities.
